content.comment_body: Hello everyone! I'm new here, though I have experience with [company_name] automation products. Recently, I purchased a [product_name] controller for a home project. Programming with [product_name] [product_name] software was intuitive, especially using ladder diagrams. Later, I tried connecting the [product_name] module to my home modem (D-Link) over WiFi, but couldn’t get it working despite trying multiple configurations. Researching forum discussions—including one that explained the process for a previous module version ([url])—I replicated the setup: configuring IPs for my devices, forwarding port 8080 to 80 for the [product_name] module, and ensuring correct gateway and netmask settings. In the [product_name] programming software, I enabled server connection options and downloaded the project to the controller, yet access through both the mobile app and web server failed when using WiFi. Only in one scenario (using a secondary LAN segment with different IPs) did the web server work but only from my laptop, not my smartphone. Any advice would be greatly appreciated!

Hi [user_name], Review the [product_name] manual ([document]), Chapter 5, and verify if both your computer browser and mobile device support the web server feature. For remote access, it's important to use TCP port 8080. Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are facing challenges connecting a [product_name] module via WiFi from smartphones, using [product_name] software and mobile apps. Standard networking and port forwarding attempts often result in success from a laptop, but not from mobile devices, revealing possible misconfigurations, compatibility concerns, and lack of clear guidance for non-PC and mobile connectivity.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect a simple and reliable WiFi connection between smartphones and the [product_name] module through the app or web portal, based on routine home router setup procedures.
